text:
alex: FYI infra CI is flaking on the gpu-provision canary. multiple GHA jobs are failing during cache restore with S3 503/SlowDowns and then terraform apply times out. example log snippet from the failing run:

```
> Restoring cache from key: infra-gcp-gpu-terraform-commit-abc123
  RequestError: send request failed
  caused by: 503 SlowDown
  github-actions/restore-cache@v3: restore failed after 3 attempts
  => terraform init completes but plan/apply later errors with 'Error: locking state: query timed out'
```

alex: this started after we ramped up matrix concurrency for gpu canaries last night (x6). seems correlated with a burst of cache restores and provider registry hits.

ci-bot: build #4821 failed — canary provisioning aborted (exit 1) :x:

jin: sounds like S3 throttling + runners hammering remote backend/registry. two quick ideas: reduce parallelism for infra workflows (concurrency groups) and add exponential backoff + more cache retry attempts. also consider changing cache key strategy so restores are less hot (use branch+sha+job-id).

sam: +1. short term patch: add `concurrency: group: infra-provision-${{ github.ref }}` to the workflow to limit parallel applies to 1-2. long term: add jitter/backoff in restore step and fallback to skipping cache on 5xx to avoid the whole job failing.

maria: we also saw registry timeouts yesterday (provider downloads). can we enable registry mirroring for terraform providers or pin a local artifact mirror? that will cut down external egress spikes during matrix runs.

alex: i pushed a test branch with two changes: 1) reduce matrix max-parallel to 2, 2) add retry wrapper around cache restore:

```
steps:
  - name: restore cache
    uses: actions/cache@v3
    with:
      path: .terraform
      key: infra-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/*.tf') }}-${{ github.run_id }}
    retry:
      max_attempts: 6
      backoff: exponential
```

opsbot: incident INC-4567 opened against infra-ci: "s3 slowdowns causing terraform lock/timeouts" — priority P2. linked runs: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/4821

ci-bot: re-run #4822 started (after concurrency change). cache restore succeeded once but terraform apply still hit state lock timeouts (backend queries failing). new log:

```
Error: Provider registry request failed: context deadline exceeded
Terraform will retry, but state operations failed: rpc timeout acquiring state lock
```

jin: backend/state is another choke point. two more options: increase state lock timeout in backend config, and add more aggressive retry/backoff for state lock acquisition. also consider batching canary runs to avoid concurrent state operations (apply/plan overlap).

sam: there’s also a cost/ops angle — we’re seeing a lot of transient burst traffic from many repos at once. talk to platform-costs about raising S3 request quota for the bucket or adding a short-lived warm pool of pre-warmed runners to smooth hits. but quota increases take time.

alex: plan: open PR with (A) workflow concurrency group, (B) actions/cache retries + jitter, (C) terraform backend tweaks (longer lock timeouts + retry). i will also file a support ticket with the object storage team to check bucket-level throttling and request rate limits.

maria: for the provider mirror: i'll prototype an internal registry mirror and a terraform CLI wrapper to prefer the mirror. that should cut external 3rd-party latency.

alex: quick mitigation PR created: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2345 — rolling out to a single canary pipeline now. monitoring logs and will post updates.

sam: nice. also add a post-merge workflow that runs terraform init/plan sequentially (no matrix) to validate the backend before any apply.

alex: opened INC-4567 and PR 2345. will keep this thread updated. tagging @maria for mirror prototype and @jin for retry/backoff review. :thumbsup:

maria: ack — will start mirror work this afternoon.

jin: i'll review the PR and suggest a provider mirror config + make the retry library shared in our devx-action repo.

alex: thanks everyone — monitoring the canary now. if things still fail we'll temporarily move canaries to a single dedicated runner pool to avoid noisy neighbors.
